nexigon_api.devices.ClaimDeviceOperation.description:
**Group `device`:** Part of the Device API, which Nexigon Agent and other software on devices use. Changes remain backward compatible for at least five years.

Claim device operation work for a device.

Leases pending work items to the device atomically, so no other worker receives
them at the same time. Report the outcome of each item with
`devices_ReportOperationStep`, passing the item's claim ID. Only the device itself
can claim its work.

nexigon_api.devices.DeviceOperationWaitF.description:

not reported a property yet, keeps the step waiting. The step shows the
latest error.

The token is a JWT signed by Nexigon Hub that carries the device ID and the given
claims. An external backend validates it with `devices_ValidateDeviceToken`.

**Note: Only use this action for integration with external systems.** The token
does not replace the credentials a device uses to connect to Nexigon Hub.

Publish events of a device.

Nexigon Hub stores events as a history of device behavior. Each event has an ID
that is unique per device. An event published again with the same ID is not
stored again, so publishing can safely be retried.

nexigon_api.devices.ReportDeviceOperatio.description:
**Group `device`:** Part of the Device API, which Nexigon Agent and other software on devices use. Changes remain backward compatible for at least five years.

Report the result of a device operation step.

Repeating a report after it was already applied is a successful no-op. A report whose
claim has been superseded is also ignored, so an expired worker cannot overwrite the
current attempt.

nexigon_api.devices.SetDeviceProfilesAct.description:

The device applies the profiles in the given order, so later profiles take
precedence. Device credentials cannot change profiles.

nexigon_api.devices.SetDevicePropertyAct.description:
**Group `device`:** Part of the Device API, which Nexigon Agent and other software on devices use. Changes remain backward compatible for at least five years.

Set a property of a device.

A property is a named JSON value of a device. Setting a property replaces the
device's own value and increments the property's version. With an expected version,
the property is only updated if its version still matches (compare-and-swap).
Devices cannot change protected properties.

nexigon_api.devices.UpdateDeviceGroupAct.description: Replace group metadata while retaining its identity and assignments.

nexigon_api.devices.UpdateDeviceGroupsAc.description:
Atomically add and remove memberships on explicit devices in one project.

Adding an existing membership or removing an absent one is a no-op. A group
cannot appear in both lists. Unrelated memberships are preserved. All devices
and groups must belong to the project; otherwise no memberships change.
Device credentials cannot change groups. Removing a membership does not cancel
work that an operation has already assigned to the device.

nexigon_api.devices.UpdateDeviceProfiles.description:
**Unstable (feature `device_profiles`).**

Atomically add and remove profiles on explicit devices in one project.

Added profiles apply after the device's other profiles, in the given order.
Adding an assigned profile keeps its position but sets its mode, and removing
an absent one is a no-op. A profile cannot appear in both lists. All devices
and profiles must belong to the project; otherwise no assignments change.
Device credentials cannot change profiles.

nexigon_api.fleet.HaltFleetOperationActi.description:
Halt a running fleet operation.

The operation selects no targets, releases no stages, and hands out no work
until it is resumed. Devices can still report the results of work that they
already claimed. The clocks of spreads, soak times, timeouts, and deadlines
do not advance while the operation is halted. Halting a halted operation has
no effect.

nexigon_api.fleet.PreviewFleetOperationT.description:
Preview the devices that a target selector currently matches.

A preview does not decide the targets of an operation. An operation selects
its targets when it starts and, if it is dynamic, periodically afterwards.

**Unstable (feature `app_updates`).**

Removal of old versions of an app.

After switching an app to a new version, the integration removes old versions

nexigon_api.properties.AppUpdateConfig.description:
**Unstable (feature `app_updates`).**

App update configuration (`dev.nexigon.apps.config`).

Desired state of the apps on a device. The integration manages the apps listed
in `apps` and leaves other installed apps untouched. Removing an app from
`apps` ends its management without uninstalling it. To uninstall an app, set
its `state` to `removed`.

The policies `hold`, `window`, `retry`, `spread`, and `gc` apply to every app
that does not set its own. They govern version changes. Changes of an app's
`state` apply at the next check.

nexigon_api.properties.AppUpdateState.description:
**Unstable (feature `app_updates`).**

State of an app's update process.

The resting states are `idle`, `completed`, `failed`, and `blocked`.

nexigon_api.properties.AppUpdateStatus.description:
**Unstable (feature `app_updates`).**

App update status (`dev.nexigon.apps.status`).

Actual state of the apps on a device, published by its app integration.

The integration writes the status with the version it read last
(compare-and-swap), so that it does not overwrite concurrent changes. Other
writers may only clear the `failure_count` and `next_attempt_at` of an app,
which requests a new attempt.

nexigon_api.properties.AppWorkloadMessag.description:
**Unstable (feature `app_updates`).**

Explanation of an app's workload status.

nexigon_api.properties.AppWorkloadStatus.description:
**Unstable (feature `app_updates`).**

**Unstable (feature `ota_updates`).**

Optional feature of the OTA update contract.

nexigon_api.properties.OtaUpdateConfig.description:
**Unstable (feature `ota_updates`).**

OTA update configuration (`dev.nexigon.ota.config`).

Desired state of a device. Integrations apply the property to defaults
built into the image as a JSON merge patch (RFC 7396): objects merge
recursively, `null` removes a default, and any other value, including an
array, replaces the default.

nexigon_api.properties.OtaUpdateRetryPol.description:
**Unstable (feature `ota_updates`).**

Retry policy for failed update attempts.

An attempt starts when the device begins downloading a version. Failures
before that, such as an unreachable Nexigon Hub, do not count as attempts.
The delay between attempts starts at `initial_delay_secs` and doubles after
each failed attempt, up to `max_delay_secs`.

nexigon_api.properties.OtaUpdateSpread.description:
**Unstable (feature `ota_updates`).**

Spreading of updates across devices.

Each device derives its position `u` from the SHA-256 hash of
`<device-id>/<target-version-id>`: the first 8 bytes, read as a big-endian
unsigned integer `n`, give `u = floor(n / 2^11) / 2^53`, which a
double-precision number represents exactly. A device may start updating to the
target once both of the following hold:

- With `duration_secs`, its turn has begun at
`start + floor(duration_secs * sqrt(u))`. The share of eligible devices
thus grows quadratically from 0 at the start to 1 after `duration_secs`.
- With `percentage`, its position is below `percentage / 100`.

nexigon_api.properties.OtaUpdateState.description:
**Unstable (feature `ota_updates`).**

OTA update state.

The resting states are `idle`, `completed`, `failed`, and `blocked`.
The integration remains in one of these until the next check begins or
the blocking condition clears.

nexigon_api.properties.OtaUpdateStatus.description:
**Unstable (feature `ota_updates`).**

OTA update status (`dev.nexigon.ota.status`).

Actual state of a device, published by its update integration.

The integration writes the status with the version it read last
(compare-and-swap), so that it does not overwrite concurrent changes. Other
writers may only clear `failure_count` and `next_attempt_at`, which requests
a new attempt.

nexigon_api.properties.OtaUpdateWindow.description:
**Unstable (feature `ota_updates`).**

Maintenance window in the device's local time.

The window restricts activation, the step that interrupts the device's
operation, such as the reboot into the new version. Integrations may
download and install an update outside the window if doing so does not
interrupt operation.

Slot names, states, and health values are those of the update system.

**Group `device`:** Part of the Device API, which Nexigon Agent and other software on devices use. Changes remain backward compatible for at least five years.

Resolve a version asset by its path.

A path consists of a repository, a package, a version tag, and the asset's
filename within the version.

Within an organization, the repository is given by its path name. The
organization defaults to that of the request, which is set by an organization
API token, the `X-Nexigon-Organization` header, or the project of a device.
Without an organization, the repository is given by its slug. A repository ID
resolves in both cases.

nexigon_api.repositories.SealPackageVers.description:
Permanently seal a version. Requires permission to manage versions.
Sealing cancels scheduled deletion and blocks changes to the name, metadata,
base version, and attachments, as well as deletion of the version, package,
or repository.
Tags remain editable. Sealing cannot be reversed.

nexigon_api.repositories.SetPackageVersi.description: Set metadata on a package version asset.

Set or clear the base of a package version. Requires permission to manage versions.

The base must belong to the same package, must not be scheduled for deletion, and
must not lead back to the version through its own bases. Sealed versions reject
changes to their base.

Schedule or cancel automatic deletion. Requires permission to manage versions.
Deletion removes the version and all tags, including locked tags. It does not
check device installations. Unused assets follow the repository cleanup policy.
A version that is the base of another version cannot be scheduled.

Set the name of a package version.
Replace the package retention policy. Requires permission to manage versions.

**Group `admin`:** Part of the Admin API, which requires instance administrator permissions. Backward-incompatible changes are more frequent than for other actions.

Deactivate a user account.

Admin-only operation. Deactivated users cannot sign in and their API tokens
are rejected. All existing sessions of the user are terminated. Memberships,
tokens, and data are retained and usable again after reactivation. Deactivating
a deactivated user replaces their message, or selects the default message if
`message` is absent. Users cannot deactivate themselves.

nexigon_api.vulnerabilities.IndexPackage.description:
**Unstable (feature `vulnerability_management`).**

Trigger indexing of every CycloneDX or SPDX document referenced by the
package's metadata via `relations.{vex}` (typically just VEX).

Mirrors `IndexVersionDocumentsAction`. Used after attaching a new
package-level VEX asset and pointing the package's metadata at it.

nexigon_api.vulnerabilities.IndexVersion.description:
**Unstable (feature `vulnerability_management`).**

Trigger indexing of every CycloneDX or SPDX document referenced by the
version's artifact assets via `relations.{sbom,vdr,vex}`.

The hub fetches the referenced documents from the repository's S3
storage and rebuilds the index for this version. The repository
must have S3 configured.
